documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Citizens Development Business Finance PLC (CDB), a licensed finance company (NBFI) -- this filing presents a single set of statements (no separate Group/Company columns), entered as basis=GROUP per this project's convention for single-entity filings. Mapped per the project's bank/NBFI convention: revenue = 'Total Operating Income' (8,857,102, the filing's own top-line subtotal after net interest income + fee income + other operating income); operating_profit = 'Operating profit before taxes on financial services' (2,064,156), the company's own subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- 'Interest expense' (4,409,502) is already netted into revenue via Net Interest Income, so a separate finance-cost figure would double count. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split, and 'Loans and receivables to customers' (180,923,555) is the core lending book, not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks and financial institutions' (88,715,600); long_term_borrowings = 'Subordinated debts' (10,833,066). 'Deposits from customers' (93,011,733) is customer deposit funding and is deliberately excluded from borrowings per project convention. Lease liabilities (1,125,910) also excluded, consistent with how this project has treated small lease liabilities for other NBFIs this session. shares_in_issue = 613,929,560 voting + 103,436,680 non-voting = 717,366,240 combined (both classes rank pari passu for EPS purposes here) -- cross-checked against Net Assets Value per share of Rs.40.60 (29,123,311k / 717,366,240 = Rs.40.60, ties exactly) and against disclosed Basic EPS of Rs.1.40 (1,001,720k / 717,366,240 = Rs.1.396, ties). No column-swap issues found. capex = 'Purchase of property, plant and equipment' per the cash flow statement (645,900).

interim_updates.note_text: CDB's Total Operating Income grew 12% YoY to Rs.4,447.6mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026; Q1 FY2025/26: Rs.3,963.5mn), with Net Interest Income up 15% (Rs.3,082.2mn to Rs.3,554.7mn) as interest income grew 33% (Rs.6,000.2mn to Rs.7,964.2mn) against a 51% rise in interest expense (Rs.2,918.0mn to Rs.4,409.5mn) -- funding costs are rising faster than asset yields, a margin-compression signal (Net Interest Margin fell to 6.43% from 7.10% at FY2025/26 year-end). By segment, growth was led by the 'Loans and advances' book: segment interest income +64.4% YoY (Rs.2,520.9mn to Rs.4,143.9mn) and segment assets +56.5% (Rs.64,684.3mn to Rs.101,224.6mn), well ahead of the 'Lease and stock out on hire' segment (+13.0% interest income, +34.9% assets) and the 'Others' segment, which shrank slightly (-7.8% interest income). Impairment charges and other credit losses fell 39.5% YoY (Rs.239.9mn to Rs.145.0mn), which flattered reported profit growth even as underlying asset quality metrics moved the other way: Gross NPA ratio rose from 3.78% (31 March 2026) to 4.51%, Net NPA ratio from 1.53% to 2.37%, and Provision Coverage Ratio fell from 60.43% to 48.58% over the same three months. Operating expenses grew 18% (Rs.1,890.1mn to Rs.2,238.4mn), driven by Personnel expenses (+24.5%, Rs.810.3mn to Rs.1,009.2mn) and Premises/equipment/establishment expenses (+12.3%, Rs.895.6mn to Rs.1,006.0mn), pushing the Cost to Income Ratio up to 50.33% from 46.64% at FY2025/26 year-end. PBT grew 14% to Rs.1,430.2mn and PAT grew 14% to Rs.1,001.7mn (Rs.875.8mn a year earlier).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for CDB -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Balance-sheet/asset-quality ratios above compare 30.06.2026 against 31.03.2026 (the filing's own balance-sheet comparative, a 3-month gap) rather than against 30.06.2025, since that is the only balance-sheet comparative the filing provides; P&L figures compare against the genuine prior-year quarter (30.06.2025) throughout.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline PBT/PAT growth (+14%) is real, driven by strong 'Loans and advances' segment growth (+64% interest income), but it is partly aided by a 39.5% YoY fall in the impairment charge even as asset-quality ratios deteriorated over the same quarter (Gross NPA 3.78% to 4.51%, Provision Coverage 60.43% to 48.58%) -- a lower quarterly impairment charge alongside rising NPA ratios and falling coverage is worth watching, since it suggests the P&L impairment charge may understate the true credit trend rather than confirm improving asset quality. Net interest margin compression (7.10% to 6.43%) is a second genuine headwind, as funding costs are rising faster than asset yields.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Total Operating Income +12% YoY to Rs.4,447.6mn; PBT +14% to Rs.1,430.2mn; PAT +14% to Rs.1,001.7mn
Net Interest Margin compressed to 6.43% (from 7.10% at FY2025/26 year-end) as interest expense grew 51% YoY against 33% interest income growth

'Loans and advances' segment interest income +64.4% YoY (Rs.2,520.9mn to Rs.4,143.9mn) and segment assets +56.5% -- the clear growth driver, well ahead of Lease/Hire Purchase (+13.0% income) and 'Others' (-7.8%)
Impairment charges fell 39.5% YoY (Rs.239.9mn to Rs.145.0mn) even as Gross NPA ratio rose from 3.78% to 4.51% and Provision Coverage Ratio fell from 60.43% to 48.58% over the same quarter
Operating expenses +18% YoY (Personnel +24.5%, Premises/equipment +12.3%), pushing Cost to Income Ratio to 50.33% from 46.64%

Core Capital (Tier I) Ratio 12.82% (min. 10%) and Total Capital Ratio 17.13% (min. 14%) remain comfortably above regulatory minimums, though both softened from 31 March 2026 (13.65% / 18.74%) as risk-weighted assets grew
key_drivers: 'Loans and advances' segment (+64.4% interest income YoY, segment assets +56.5%) is the primary driver of both revenue growth and the balance-sheet expansion this quarter, well ahead of the other two segments
Net Interest Margin compression (7.10% to 6.43%) -- interest expense (+51% YoY) is growing faster than interest income (+33% YoY) -- is a genuine headwind partly offset by strong volume growth

The 39.5% YoY fall in the impairment charge boosted reported PBT/PAT growth, but this moved in the opposite direction to asset-quality ratios (Gross NPA 3.78%->4.51%, Provision Coverage 60.43%->48.58% over the same quarter) -- the P&L charge and the balance-sheet asset-quality trend are not telling the same story this quarter
